prompt: Create a production paper texture for a lovingly weathered old Vietnamese mountain-travel diary bound in indigo cloth. A perfectly flat orthographic scan, portrait 2:3. Fill the ENTIRE canvas with paper from edge to edge, no surrounding surface, no perspective, no book mockup. Visibly aged warm tan rag paper: muted antique buff and tea-stained parchment, approximately #d7bd91 across the broad center, never white or pale cream. Beautiful fine cellulose fibers, soft uneven grain and gentle desaturated umber mottling. This should look like paper that has traveled in a backpack for decades, tactile and poetic, not a Halloween scroll. The large central 84 percent is spacious, evenly illuminated and has low-contrast grain, keeping dark handwritten Vietnamese text clearly readable. All strong wear stays in the narrow outside margins: frayed fibers, tiny short edge tears with fine dark seams and pale exposed fibers, irregular foxing, worn corner creases, subtle old water tide marks. No dark stains crossing the center. No text, writing, letters, ruled lines, numbers, illustrations, symbols, photographs, objects, hands, folds across the center, or decorative border. No white vignette or white center, no glows. Not scorched, no burnt black edge. Watercolor-adjacent material realism, very high quality, quietly beautiful, natural dry matte paper, uniform flat lighting. This is the RIGHT leaf: binding is at the LEFT edge. Fine compressed binding fibers and a softly darker narrow crease only along the leftmost 2 percent. The RIGHT outer edge has distinct small nicks and fine short tears; a faint repaired crease and a tiny softened split at the lower-right corner. A few faded foxing flecks hug the top-right margin. Different naturally placed marks from the left leaf, same warm tan stock and tone. The paper completely fills the rectangular canvas, tiny tears are material detail within the margins, no outside background.
